verdicts.note: No abstract; SSRN preprint of the gated anchor 'Fertility, Household Structure, and Parental Labor Supply: Evidence from Rural China'. Duplicate of the JCE version.
No abstract; self-employment earnings differentials among millennials.

No abstract, but the title is remarkable and squarely on §4's enumeration: 'GEOLOGY, HOUSEHOLD FORMATION RULES and the Demand for Sons in Vietnam'. Geology as a plausibly exogenous determinant of household formation rules is a design the scope never imagined. Priority trace -- if it delivers, it is the only geographic instrument for the arrangement in the frame.
No abstract; relational contracts for household formation, fertility choice and separation. Formal theory linking the arrangement decision to fertility.
Japanese midlife women sandwiched between mothers-in-law and children.
Flexible work arrangements and work-family balance among South African fathers.
Ageing policy for traditional and blended families.

'Do parents matter?' Multidimensional INTERGENERATIONAL TIES against married women's intended and ideal family size in Jiangsu, an extremely low-fertility Chinese province. Directly on the extended arm's estimand, with the parents' own preferences among the measured dimensions -- which is the mechanism the mother-in-law records describe qualitatively.
Filial end-of-life care and declining multigenerational co-residence under rural-urban migration in China.
ECHR jurisprudence on surrogacy and personal identity.
Youth occupational status by social origin and sibship size, explicitly REGARDLESS of co-residence in the parental household. Employment outcome.
Microsimulation of kin sets and co-habitation patterns in the old-Polish peasant family. Same demographic-availability constraint as the Eastern European record in batch 16.
Out-of-home care for children in India.
Paediatric palliative care.
Ageing and the changing family role in Sri Lanka.
Peruvian legal analysis of paternity leave for breastfeeding.

Validation of the OWN-CHILDREN METHOD against the German Mikrozensus. A measurement warning: own-children fertility estimates depend on the child CO-RESIDING with the mother, so in a chapter about co-residence the measurement error is correlated with the exposure. Carry to extraction.

Co-residence between adult family members as RECIPROCAL SUPPORT, distinguishing an adult child supported by a parent from a parent living in the child's household -- §6's dependency-direction distinction, measured. French Family and Housing survey linked to the 2011 census.
No abstract; regional differences in Japanese female labour force participation.
Family and friends in personal networks over the life course, Switzerland.

'Do housing options affect child birth decisions?' Taiwan PSFD panel, with the option set spanning RENTING, OWNING, LIVING WITH PARENTS OR SIBLINGS, living in a house bought by parents, and staff housing, against fertility decisions. Tenure and the arrangement in ONE choice set with a birth outcome -- the single best record for adjudicating Wall 1 empirically rather than by ruling. Priority read for the second-read packet.
Authors' response on out-of-home placement for children with disabilities.
No abstract; chapter titled 'Young Adulthood'.
Reference entry 'Household Economics', no abstract.

FINANCIALLY DEPENDENT CHILDREN and parental RETIREMENT postponement. The parents'-side cost of extended dependency, now the fifth record framing the arrangement from the parents' budget rather than the young adult's autonomy.
No abstract; the policy context of fertility in SPAIN. The registered setting and a policy framing; trace for whether housing or youth-transition policy features.
Entrepreneurial behaviour of rural Indian women.
'Long-term Care: The Persistence of Familialism' in SPAIN, opening on the low-fertility equilibrium. Familialism is the norm variable the pre-launch arm invokes, but the object here is elder care.
ISSP social networks dataset record.
Longevity and senescence in wild African elephants.
No abstract; early adultification among homeless young people. Forced early home-leaving, no fertility outcome visible.

Published version of the 20-country optimal-matching analysis: employment, LEAVING HOME, union formation, marriage and CHILDBEARING as one sequence, men and women over 35, European Social Survey. The sequence approach at the largest scale in the frame.
No abstract; precocious transitions and heroin use among gang-affiliated men.
No abstract; children's street movement in Bangladesh.
No abstract; pregnancy and childbearing among cohabiting versus married couples. A.7's union-type question.
Instability in PARENT-CHILD co-residence and adolescent development in urban South Africa. The child's co-residence with a parent, and a development outcome.
Living arrangements and caregiving to older adults in India.
Entry into a CORESIDENTIAL UNION and changes in commuting time. Co-residence with a partner, commuting as outcome.
No abstract; age heterogamy in Bangladeshi marriage.

FIXED-EFFECT 2SLS on Japanese prefectural data linking marital status, the fertility rate and socioeconomic factors, reporting that the MALE CO-RESIDENCE RATE has a positive effect. A pre-launch arrangement variable inside an instrumented aggregate model -- rare in this arm, though the unit is the prefecture rather than the person. Priority read for the identification strategy.
No abstract; determinants of child abuse in Colombia.

No abstract; 'The Intergenerational Effect and Second Childbirth' in Shaanxi. Names an intergenerational exposure and a parity-specific birth outcome; trace for whether the exposure is co-residence or preference.
Structural biology of sperm-egg recognition. The 'fertilization' homonym at its purest.
News piece on the same sperm-egg structure.
Third record of the IZUMO1-JUNO complex.

Whether rising INTERGENERATIONAL CO-RESIDENCE and financial dependency among young Black and White women are associated with declining marriage and rising NONMARITAL PARENTHOOD, US Census and ACS 1970-2010. Forty years of the exposure and a fertility outcome in one series, with a race split -- and it explicitly entertains the reverse arrow, that parenthood drives the co-residence.
Teenage mothers' perspectives on early parenthood.

Educational and racial differences in EXTENDED KIN COUNTS in the US. Kin availability is the constraint on the extended arm's exposure -- the demographic-availability point again, now for a contemporary setting.

Whether young MOTHERS and FATHERS differ in RETURNING HOME, with their own children's co-residence among the predictors, NLSY. Parenthood drives the arrangement here -- threat 2, measured, with a gender split.
No abstract; number of children living at home as a risk factor for abandoning cryopreserved embryos. A.17's.
Image-tracing surveillance for elders living at home.

'Delayed and depressed: from expensive housing to smaller families' -- a framework in which housing acts on LEAVING THE PARENTAL HOME, partnering and having children, all of which extend later in life. Wall 1's mechanism stated as a framework; belongs in the second-read packet.
Qatar's HOUSING WELFARE SYSTEM against family formation and dissolution. A policy that allocates housing to families -- design 3's shape in a setting the frame lacks entirely.
Role balance among sandwich-generation Australian women.
Marital status, CHILD PROXIMITY and older adults' health in China. Proximity as exposure, health as outcome, elderly population.
